title: Saudi Arabia Completes $55 Billion EA Takeover in Largest Leveraged Buyout Ever
excerpt: The Public Investment Fund now owns 93.4% of Electronic Arts after clearing all regulatory hurdles, with Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners holding a 1.1% stake in the gaming giant.
body:
• Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has completed its $55 billion acquisition of Electronic Arts, making it the largest leveraged buyout in history.
  • PIF owns 93.4% of the company, with Silver Lake holding 5.5% and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners at 1.1%.
  • The deal cleared its final regulatory hurdle on July 30 when the European Commission approved it under EU foreign subsidy rules.
  • EA will remain headquartered in Redwood City, California, with CEO Andrew Wilson staying on to lead the company.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund closed its $55 billion acquisition of Electronic Arts on August 4, completing the largest leveraged buyout in history and giving the sovereign wealth fund control of franchises including Madden NFL, EA Sports FC, The Sims, Battlefield, and Mass Effect.

The deal, first announced on September 29, 2025, was structured as an all-cash buyout at $210 per share — a 25% premium over EA's pre-announcement trading price. JPMorgan Chase arranged more than $20 billion in debt financing for the transaction, pushing EA's total debt from $2.2 billion to roughly $20 billion.

A Consortium With Political Connections

The buying consortium comprises three entities: PIF, which emerges with 93.4% ownership according to a Brazilian regulatory filing; private equity firm Silver Lake with 5.5%; and Affinity Partners, the investment firm founded by Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, with 1.1%.

According to the Financial Times, the deal originated in August 2025 when Kushner approached Silver Lake co-CEO Egon Durban about a potential acquisition. Kushner used his ties to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to secure PIF's backing, and later brought in JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon for the debt financing.

"The Commission concluded that the notified transaction would not raise competition concerns, given its limited impact on competition in the markets where the companies are active."

— European Commission, antitrust review statement

The deal drew scrutiny in Washington. Democratic senators Richard Blumenthal and Elizabeth Warren wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and EA CEO Andrew Wilson in October 2025, raising concerns about potential foreign influence through consumer data. Multiple individuals who spoke to the Financial Times, however, said the deal was expected to pass U.S. regulatory review "easily," given Kushner's relationship with both Trump and Crown Prince Mohammed.

Regulatory Path and Final Clearances

The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States cleared the transaction when the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired on February 9, 2026. The European Commission gave antitrust approval on July 23, finding no competition concerns. The final hurdle — a review under the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation, designed to prevent unfair non-EU subsidies from distorting competition — was cleared on July 30.

EA confirmed in a regulatory filing that all required approvals had been obtained as of that date, setting August 4 as the closing date.

Saudi Vision 2030 and the Gaming Bet

The acquisition is the most ambitious move yet in Saudi Arabia's push to become what Crown Prince Mohammed has called a "global hub for games and esports" by 2030. PIF already held a 10% stake in EA before the deal and owns Savvy Games Group, the kingdom's dedicated gaming investment arm. The fund also holds shares in Take-Two Interactive, the publisher behind Grand Theft Auto.

According to Reuters, PIF views EA's sports portfolio — particularly EA Sports FC, the successor to the FIFA-branded football games — as an asset worth holding for the long term, aligning with the kingdom's broader investments in global football and sports entertainment.

Concerns Over Creative Control and Jobs

The deal has not been without controversy. Content creators for The Sims expressed concerns that the franchise's emphasis on LGBTQ inclusivity could be affected under Saudi ownership, given the kingdom's record on LGBTQ rights. Several prominent Sims creators, including Kayla Sims, James Turner, and Jesse McNamara, left EA's creator program. Developer Maxis issued a statement in January 2026 pledging that the game's values and creative control would remain "unchanged."

The $20 billion debt load has also raised concerns. The Verge reported that the leveraged structure could force layoffs, reduced budgets, and less creative risk-taking. United Videogame Workers-CWA, a union representing EA employees, criticized the potential for job cuts to "pad investor pockets."

What's Next

EA will remain headquartered in Redwood City, California, and Andrew Wilson will continue as CEO. As a private company, EA will no longer report quarterly earnings publicly, giving its new owners more latitude to pursue long-term strategies without the pressure of public market expectations.

The transaction ranks as the second-largest gaming acquisition ever, behind Microsoft's $75.4 billion purchase of Activision Blizzard in 2023, and is expected to accelerate consolidation in an industry still recovering from a prolonged post-pandemic downturn.
nri_angle: Indian gamers and the large Indian diaspora tech workforce in the U.S. may feel the effects as EA navigates its new ownership structure, particularly if cost-cutting measures impact the company's studios or workforce.
